newsItems.headline: Gold recovers from two-week low ahead of US inflation - Reuters
UK's FTSE 100 flat as energy gains counter mining losses amid US-Iran flare-up - Reuters

riskTone.label: NEUTRAL
riskTone.rationale: FTSE flat with sector rotation; US-Iran flare-up adds mild risk-off, offset by energy gains; gold recovery signals modest caution.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the currency picture — GBP/USD is up +0.22% today, which sits at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range (meaning sterling is near its strongest recently), and because UK100 and sterling move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes FTSE's big dollar-earners worth less in sterling terms), this is a mild headwind for the index; however the model rates the overall FX impact as NEUTRAL since the move is modest. The dominant forces today are the commodity sectors: Brent crude is surging +3.86% (linked to a US-Iran flare-up reported ~17 hours ago per Reuters, which has lifted oil prices), directly boosting Shell and BP which are top-5 index weights, making ENERGY firmly BULLISH; copper is up +1.60%, which is BULLISH for miners like Rio Tinto and Glencore as copper acts as a fast-read on global growth appetite. Banks are NEUTRAL as the 10-year gilt yield [the interest rate the UK government pays to borrow for 10 years] is barely moved (-2bp), and importantly there is no long-end gilt stress [no sharp sell-off in longer-dated UK government bonds that would signal fiscal panic]. US futures are almost flat (S&P 500 +0.07%) and the VIX [a measure of expected stock market volatility — lower = calmer] is at 17.75, a NORMAL regime, so there is no US-driven fear dampening things. European markets (DAX, EuroStoxx) are both slightly negative (-0.18%/-0.20%), acting as a mild drag. The ORB [Opening Range Breakout — a trade strategy that waits for price to break above or below the range set in the first 15 minutes after the 08:00 London open] has already broken to the DOWN side this morning, with the index gapping down ~62 points from last night's close and price sitting at 10,429 — below both the ORB low of 10,447 and the overnight low of 10,415 is the next floor to watch, with the prior day low at 10,443 already breached. The 14-day average daily range [the typical distance the index travels from high to low over two weeks] is 128 points, and today has already used 69% of that — meaning there is statistically less room left to run, which reduces the appeal of chasing a big directional move late in the session. The headline risk is significant: US CPI [the main US inflation reading] is due at 13:30 BST today — this is the single biggest scheduled event of the week and could sharply move sterling, gilts, US futures, and therefore UK100 in either direction; a hotter-than-expected print would likely push the dollar up, sterling down, which perversely would be BULLISH for FTSE via the sign-flip, while a cool print does the reverse. UK GDP is also due Wednesday 07:00 BST (two days away), so build caution into any overnight holds. Despite the commodity tailwind from energy and miners giving a bias score of +3 (mildly bullish), the already-broken-down ORB, the 69% ADR already consumed, and the looming 13:30 CPI release make this a LOW-CONVICTION setup — confidence is rated 4/10; a clean break back above the ORB high at 10,488 post-CPI would flip the view bullish, while a sustained hold below the overnight low of 10,415 would confirm the bearish momentum. For the ORB trader specifically, today looks like a STAND-ASIDE or at most a cautious short-bias day given the downside break is live but range is largely spent and a high-impact data event at 13:30 creates serious two-way risk — the cleanest approach is to respect the downside break but tighten targets and avoid holding through CPI. Key levels: ORB high 10,488 (resistance), ORB low 10,447 (broken, now resistance), overnight low 10,415 (next support), prior day low 10,443, with 10,400 as the psychological level below; to the upside, prior day high 10,526 is the ceiling. Remember: the ORB broke down but 70% of the day's typical range is already gone — fade the chase, respect CPI at 13:30.
